facts.statement: The type species of the genus Buchanosteus is Buchanosteus confertituberculatus, described by Chapman in 1916.
A species named Buchanosteus nuricus was described by Mark-Kurik in 2004.
A species named Buchanosteus guangxiensis was described by Wang in 2005.
Fossils of Buchanosteus have been found in Early Devonian marine strata across Asia and Australia.
facts.quote: Its fossils have been found in Early Devonian-aged marine strata throughout Asia and Australia.

facts.statement: The type species B. confertituberculatus is known from the Emsian-aged Taemas-Weejasper Reef in modern-day New South Wales, Australia.
facts.quote: Buchanosteus confertituberculatus, the type species, is known from several specimens found from the Emsian-aged Taemas-Weejasper Reef in what is now New South Wales, Australia.

facts.statement: B. confertituberculatus lived alongside other buchanosteid genera in the same area.
facts.quote: It coexisted sympatrically with other buchanosteid genera there.

facts.statement: B. guangxianensis is known mainly from an incomplete endocranium found in Pragian-aged deposits near Guangxi, China.
facts.quote: Buchanosteus guangxianensis is known primarily from a well-preserved, albeit incomplete endocranium from Pragian-aged deposits near Guangxi, China.

facts.statement: B. guangxianensis is compared to the large buchanosteid Exutaspis from the late Emsian Wuding Formation in Yunnan.
facts.quote: It is compared to another buchanosteid, the "giant" Exutaspis from the late Emsian Wuding Formation in Yunnan.

facts.statement: B. nuricus is anatomically very similar to B. confertituberculatus.
facts.quote: Is very similar in anatomy to B. confertituberculatus

facts.statement: The parent group of the genus Buchanosteus is the family Buchanosteidae.
Buchanosteus belongs to the class Placodermi.
Buchanosteus lived during the Emsian stage, between 410.62 and 393.47 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Emsian to Emsian (410.62 to 393.47 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Buchanosteus is an extinct genus of arthrodire placoderm.
rejected.quote: Buchanosteus is an extinct genus of arthrodire placoderm.

rejected.statement: B. nuricus is known from one or two specimens found in Emsian strata in the Qaranghandy Region of Kazakhstan, named after the Nura River.
rejected.quote: Buchanosteus nuricus is known from one or two specimens from Emsian strata in the Qaranghandy Region in Kazakhstan, and named for the Nura River.
